acceptance: Exactly one function in the tree decides whether a Go walk skips a directory, and each whole-tree walker calls it.
A table test pins the rule for testdata, vendor, a dot name, an underscore name and a normal name.
The whole-tree guards (rawgitratchet, sizeratchet, emptytests) give the same results before and after the change.
fix: Give the rule one home, an exported predicate in a small package that every whole-tree walker imports. Replace the five copies with it in one refactor commit. Keep envscope.SkipDir separate only if its rule really differs, and name the difference in its package note.
source: console 2026-11-23: round-1 review of the empty-test guard (c13), MEDIUM M1, declined in that change as a separate refactor
summary: The rule for which directories a Go source walk skips (testdata, vendor, and names that start with a dot or an underscore) has five private copies: rawgitratchet, sizeratchet, coversplit, emptytests, and a different rule in envscope.SkipDir. A change to the go tool's ignore rule must be made five times, and the copies can drift.
title: One shared rule for the directories a Go tree walk skips
